# Frontend UI Engineering Skill for Muse

A complete operating manual for building production-quality, accessible, responsive user interfaces with an agent: component architecture (colocated files, composition over configuration, focused components, data fetching separated from presentation), a state-management ladder (local state → lifted state → context → URL state → server state → global store), and design-system adherence with a reference-led process for finding a real visual direction. Its signature section is the anti-"AI aesthetic" playbook — it names the tells (purple/indigo everything, excessive gradients, rounded-2xl on everything, generic hero sections, stock card grids, shadow-heavy design) and replaces each with production-grade alternatives. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility (keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, focus management in dialogs, meaningful empty and error states), mobile-first responsive design with concrete breakpoints, skeleton loading and optimistic updates, plus two brutally honest tables — "Common Rationalizations" (why "we'll make it responsive later" is a lie) and "Red Flags" — ending with a verification checklist before anything ships. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: the code examples are React/TSX-flavored (Tailwind classes, hooks) — the principles are framework-agnostic, but you'll translate the idioms if your stack differs; it also demands real standards (axe-core, keyboard testing), so shipping "good enough" isn't its vocabulary. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it...
